name: Deploy

require.label: define target, environments, pipeline, secrets & release
lock at least one dependency in the manifest

blurb: How each service ships — target, environments, pipeline, secrets, release — and the libraries it depends on.
prompt:
Define how this project SHIPS and what it DEPENDS ON — the two halves of getting it running.

**1. Shipping**, per service (one per linked repo): the deploy TARGET (hosting platform + workload —
static / serverless / container / long-running), the ENVIRONMENT ladder (dev → staging → prod, each
mapped to a branch), the CI/CD PIPELINE (build → test → deploy, with the gating stage), CONFIG +
SECRETS per environment (names only — values live in the host vault), the RELEASE strategy
(recreate / rolling / blue-green / canary) + rollback policy, and HEALTH checks / observability.
Record it with `bsc-plan deploy set` (config JSON on stdin) — that fills the Deploy pane; `bsc-plan
deploy get` shows it.

**2. Dependencies** — lock the libraries every repo needs ONCE, here, so the parallel fleet never
each adds and redefines them in their own worktrees (which collide at integration). Write them to
`dependencies.json`:
```json
{
  "registries": { "internal": { "url": "https://npm.internal/", "scope": "@acme", "auth": "INTERNAL_NPM_TOKEN" } },
  "dependencies": [
    { "repo": "owner/app", "ecosystem": "npm",   "name": "zod",       "version": "^3.23", "why": "schema validation" },
    { "repo": "owner/app", "ecosystem": "npm",   "name": "@acme/ui",  "version": "^2",   "source": "internal", "why": "design system" },
    { "repo": "owner/api", "ecosystem": "cargo", "name": "serde",     "version": "1",      "why": "(de)serialization" }
  ]
}
```
Per dependency: `repo` (`owner/repo`; omit ⇒ every repo of that ecosystem), `ecosystem` (`npm` or
`cargo`), `name`, `version` (omit ⇒ latest), `dev` (test-only), `why`, and `source` — the registry
KEY when it does NOT come from the public default (npm registry / crates.io). Define each non-public
registry once in `registries` (its `url`, npm `scope`, and `auth` = the SECRET NAME for its token),
and **record that same `auth` secret in the deploy secrets above** so the pipeline can fetch it.
These become each repo's real `package.json` / `Cargo.toml` (+ `.npmrc` / `.cargo/config.toml` for
private sources) at publish, and are inlined into every worker as the locked, authoritative set.
These shipping + dependency decisions become deployment ISSUES owned by a `deploy` stream at publish.

Gate: shipping defined (target per service, ≥2 environments, staged pipeline, secrets, release
strategy) AND at least one dependency locked in `dependencies.json`.
